result.summary: The import still fails correctly for a bad attachment id; this only stops ImportRecorder from error-logging that expected miss so Datadog Error Tracking goes quiet. The write-up overclaims a wrong-customer root cause and special-cases one fingerprint instead of treating expected import validation consistently.

problems.title: Symptom filter, not a policy
problems.detail: handlePendingAttachments already logs missing and wrong-customer attachments at info and returns entity_not_found. The PR only downgrades that same error in ImportRecorder, and still error-logs other expected client not-founds such as user.

problems.title: Tests restate plumbing, not the claim
problems.detail: The litest checks the public not_found/bulk_partial_failure response. The unit test only checks an explicit logLevel option. Neither asserts that importThreadMessage logs attachment misses at info.

problems.title: Root cause is not unique
problems.detail: Missing attachment ids and customer mismatches share one entity_not_found. The description asserts a wrong-customer client bug that this code cannot prove.

result.betterFix: If Error Tracking should ignore expected import validation, classify NotFound/validation failures as info inside recordFailed for every entity, and unit-test that choice on the import path. Do not add an attachment-only logLevel escape because that fingerprint appeared in Datadog.
